get.description: Checks that the API is reachable. Not needed before other calls.

Up to three reports this Book can have, the main one first, each as a request a person would type, in `language`: the Book’s groups at its first two levels, each as its natural report (income and expenses together this year, income or expenses by month, balances today), ranked by Bkper AI once each time the groups change. Periods: activity this year, or the last year with movements when this year has none (the text names that year), and balances today. Use them when the person does not know what to ask, or after `not_a_report`; to build one, send it as `prompt`, with the same `language`, and, to show it, `format: html` to `POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report`: exactly a suggestion’s text (spacing aside, case kept) is built with no AI. When the Book has no reports at all, there are none and `problem` tells why: `empty_book` (no transactions yet) or `nothing_to_report` (no groups, or most Accounts with transactions in no group); if the person may (`problem.canOrganize`), offer to help organize its groups, changing groups only, never transactions. Read-only.

post.summary: Build a financial report of a Book from a request in any language
post.description:
Builds a financial report of the Book: of one of its root groups (such as Expenses or Assets, with its subgroups and Accounts), of a group or Account the prompt names, of several side by side, or of income versus expenses, over a period of whole months, by month or not, optionally only for one `#hashtag`. Read-only: the Book is never changed.

To show a person a report, send `{ "prompt": "<their request, in their own words and language>", "format": "html" }` and give them the returned HTML file as it is: it is self-contained and interactive. With the Bkper CLI: `bkper app api request report /api/v1/books/<bookId>/report -d '{"prompt":"…","format":"html"}' > report.html`, then publish `report.html`. That one call is the whole task: do not ask for `spec` first, query the balances yourself or re-check the amounts; every amount is a Bkper balance read by code, and the file shows the query it read.

With `format: spec` (the default) the report is the JSON Report’s own web client renders: its spec (with the data of every chart that fits), intent, text, language, query, data time, chart, trace (how its charts were chosen) and link. `text` is the report’s own short text in its language; sent back as `prompt` with its `language`, it asks for the same report, and `chart` shows it as another chart. An `intent`, such as a previous report’s, builds the report without AI, and so does a suggestion’s text sent as `prompt`.

Every amount is a Bkper balance of one group or Account, as Bkper returns it (but a net result Report calculates, labelled so), read by deterministic code; balances may be up to 60 seconds old. Code finds in the prompt the exact names of the Book’s groups and Accounts it writes, and its first `#hashtag` (Bkper filters balances by one); AI only recognizes the root group when the prompt writes no such name, the parts of the period it says (how long, which year, month and quarter, and those of a period it compares with; never a date), whether it asks about months, parts, an earlier period or a bridge, and which chart it names; code decides the report and its charts from those judgments and the numbers.

It carries no trace.

code.description: What failed: `invalid_request` (400, the message names the field), `unauthorized` (401, no valid Bkper token), `forbidden` (403, the person cannot view the Book), `not_found` (404, no such API route), `book_not_found` (404, no such Book, or not shared with the person), `not_a_report` (422, the request names nothing this Book can report: ask for a root group or income versus expenses with a period, or send a suggestion), `future_period` (422, the period has not started), `unknown_root` (422, the intent names no root group of the Book), `unknown_target` (422, the intent’s `target`, or one `alongside`, is no group or Account under its root group), `mixed_targets` (422, the intent’s `alongside` mixes balances at a date, Asset and Liability, with activity in a period, Incoming and Outgoing: ask for them in separate reports), `no_net_result` (422, the Book has no net result: no group combines its Incoming and Outgoing groups, or its activity groups share Accounts; organizing its groups fixes it), `empty_book` (422, the Book has no transactions yet), `nothing_to_report` (422, the Book has no groups, or most of its Accounts with transactions are in no group; organizing them into groups fixes it), `mixed_group` (422, the group asked for holds both balances, Asset or Liability, and activity, Incoming or Outgoing; separating them into groups of their own fixes it), `ai_allowance_exhausted` (429, the person’s Bkper AI allowance is used up: suggestions sent as they are, and requests by `intent`, still work), `upstream_error` (502, Bkper or Bkper AI failed: try again) or `internal_error` (500).

Send it as `prompt` to ask for the same report again, or show it to the person to edit.

ReportSpec.description: The report as a flat json-render spec (`root` and `elements`) of the Report catalog, every text in `language`: `Report` (title, period, the `request` it answers as a person would type it, its period as asked, and a `notice` when it could not compare as asked) holds `Answer` (amount, previous period amount and change; one per group or Account shown side by side, in order, with none for them together), `Chart` (when one fits), `Visualizations` (every other chart that fits, with its data, and a preferred chart that does not fit with why), `BreakdownTable` (the subgroups and Accounts Bkper returns, with amount, share and change, nested; for a net result Report calculates, its roots and a total; side by side, the groups and Accounts shown, with no total) and `Source` (with `calculated` when Report calculated the net result). Every amount is a Bkper balance of one group or Account, as Bkper returns it, but a net result Report calculates. Amounts and ratios are exact decimal strings; months and instants are ISO.

root.description: Id of a root (top-level) group of the Book, as in `bkper group list`, or `net-result` for income versus expenses: the net result Bkper calculates for the root group that combines Incoming and Outgoing groups; without one, the Incoming roots minus the Outgoing roots, labelled as calculated by Report, when each root is purely Incoming or Outgoing and no two share an Account. Also the id of an Account in no group (`bkper account list`), reported alone.

target.description: Id of a group or Account under the root group, at any depth (`bkper group list`, `bkper account list`), to report instead of the whole root: its own Bkper balance and its own subgroups and Accounts, read from the root’s balances. Left out, the root. Not with `net-result` or an Account in no group.

alongside.description: More groups or Accounts to show side by side with the first (`root` and `target`), in order: each with its own Bkper balance, never added up, with no total and no shares of one. All balances at a date (Asset, Liability) or all activity in a period (Incoming, Outgoing), else `mixed_targets`. One asked for twice shows once. Only charts that imply no whole fit: by month, area, ranked bars, compared and the table; a pie, donut or stacked chart shows dimmed with why. To show their total, the person adds a group that holds them in Bkper. Not with `net-result`.

anyOf.description: A period id of older intents, still accepted.

period.description: The period, in the Book’s time zone, as its parts, as the person said them: relative words stay relative (`{ "span": "year", "year": "previous" }` is last year whenever it is read) and written years stay written (`{ "span": "quarter", "year": 2024, "quarter": 3 }` is Q3 2024). Periods are whole months: a running one (this month, quarter or year, year to date, the last 12 months) runs through the end of this month, and its comparison covers the same months; past ones are whole calendar periods. Responses always give parts; the period ids of older intents (`today`, `this_month`, `last_month`, `this_quarter`, `last_quarter`, `this_year`, `last_year`, `ytd`, `last_12_months`, `all`, a year `2025`, a quarter `2025-Q3` or a month `2025-10`) are still accepted.

monthly.description: Show the period month by month.

compareWith.description: Without `compared`, what the period is compared with: `previous`, the period right before it (December for January, the previous quarter or year; for a running period the same months of the previous one), or `year_earlier`, the same months a year earlier. A balance at a date (Asset, Liability) compares with the balance at the end of the previous period, or a year before its date. All time compares with nothing. Left out, `previous`.

view.description: The layout asked for: `trend` (over time), `breakdown` (what makes up the amount: a donut of a few parts, a pie of more, else ranked bars) or `total` (the amount alone). Left out, the report picks one.

chart.description: The chart the person asked for: `bar` or `line` (by month), `area` (by month), `stacked` (the parts by month), `ranked-bar`, `donut` or `pie` (the parts of the total), `compare` (each part against the period compared with, see `compareWith`), `table` (no chart) or `auto`. `waterfall` (a bridge) is accepted but never drawn, as its bars would not be Bkper balances: the report shows it dimmed with why. Left out or `auto`, the report picks one; a chart that does not fit the report is not drawn: the report shows the closest chart that fits, else the one it picks, and offers the asked-for chart dimmed with why (see the response’s `chart` and `trace.chart`).

hashtags.description: Only transactions with this hashtag, without `#`: at most one, as Bkper filters balances by one.

ReportIntent.description: Exactly what to report, with no AI needed: a root group (or a `target` under it), an Account in no group or `net-result`, others `alongside` it, a period, whether by month, what it is compared with, an optional view, chart and hashtags. Take it from an earlier report’s `intent`.

PeriodParts.description: A period as its parts; at least one. Without `span`, a month when `month` is given, else a quarter when `quarter` is, else a year. Examples: last year `{ "span": "year", "year": "previous" }`; this year to date `{ "span": "year_to_date" }`; Q3 2024 `{ "span": "quarter", "year": 2024, "quarter": 3 }`; March `{ "span": "month", "month": 3 }`; January last year `{ "span": "month", "month": 1, "year": "previous" }`; a balance now `{ "span": "now" }`.

It must be the same kind of period: `{ "year": 2023 }` compares last year with 2023, `{ "quarter": 1 }` compares Q3 with Q1, `{ "year": 2019 }` compares January with January 2019. Named later than the period, the two swap, so change reads from the earlier to the later. A comparison of another kind, one that overlaps the period, or one with all time cannot be made: the report then compares with the previous period instead (all time with nothing) and says so (`trace.comparisonError`, and a notice in the spec). Left out, `compareWith` says what the period is compared with.

judgments.description: With a `prompt`: what Bkper AI recognized in it, each answer with its score. Code decides the report from these.

names.description: With a `prompt` that writes names of the Book’s groups or Accounts: those names, as the Book writes them, in order. The report is of them (side by side when several), not of the `root` judgment.

periodRules.description: With a `prompt`: the rules that changed the parts of the period read, in order: `span_alone` (a month, quarter or year with nothing saying which is no period), `rolling_period` (the last 12 months ignore a relative year), `kind_of_period` (a second period said as a month and a quarter is of the period’s kind), `same_as_period` (compared parts equal to the period’s say no other period) or `previous_of_period` (the previous month or quarter of a second period is the default comparison; last year counts back from a written year).

rule.description: With a `prompt`: the first rule that applied to the judgments, in order: `named` (the chart word), `bridge` (a waterfall), `versus_earlier` (a comparison), `over_time_composition` (stacked parts), `over_time` (by month), `composition` (the parts) or `auto` (the report picks).

comparisonError.description: Present when the comparison the intent asks for cannot be made: `comparison_kind_mismatch` (another kind of period, such as a month for a year), `comparison_not_earlier` (it overlaps the period) or `comparison_unavailable` (all time has nothing before it). The report then compares with the previous period instead (all time with nothing), and the spec’s `Report` says so in its `notice`.

rows.description: Top-level parts with an amount in the period.

negative.description: Of those, the parts below zero, in the sense of the report.

mixed.description: Whether the parts are of different types, as under a mixed group or in a net result.

previous.description: Whether there is a previous period to compare with.

net.description: Whether the report is a net result (income versus expenses).

permanent.description: Whether the report is a balance at the end of the period (Assets, Liabilities) rather than activity within it.

sideBySide.description: Present when the report shows several groups or Accounts side by side (the parts are those), which are no parts of one whole.

facts.description: The facts of the report’s numbers that decide which charts fit.

items.description: A way to show the report: `bar`, `line`, `area` or `stacked` by month; `ranked-bar`, `donut` or `pie` of the parts; `compare` (each part against the previous period); `waterfall` (a bridge, never drawn: only offered dimmed when asked for); `table` (no chart).

fitting.description: Every chart that fits the report, in the order to offer them; the spec’s `Visualizations` carries the data of each.

rule.description: What chose `main`: `preference` (the intent’s `chart`, which fits), `closest` (the fitting chart closest to a preference that does not fit) or `rules` (the report’s own choice, with no preference or nothing close).

code.description: Why it does not fit: `net_result`, `negative_part` (a part below zero, `rowId`), `mixed_parts`, `few_parts`, `too_many_parts`, `few_months`, `no_amounts`, `no_previous`, `not_a_whole` (the parts Bkper returns do not add up to the total), `no_bridge` (a bridge is never drawn) or `side_by_side` (groups or Accounts side by side are no parts of one whole). `not_a_bridge` and `no_change` are no longer given.

rowId.description: The breakdown row that is the reason.

unfit.description: The preferred chart, when it does not fit the report, and why; the spec shows it dimmed with the reason in words.

chart.description: The charts that fit, and how the main one was chosen.

ReportTrace.description: How the report chose its charts: the judgments of the request and the rule they fired, then the facts of its numbers, from which code decides which charts fit.

items.description: A report this Book can have, as a person would ask for it, in the language of the suggestions. Send it as `prompt` to `POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report`, with the same `language`: exactly this text (spacing aside, case kept) builds it with no AI.

suggestions.description: With `not_a_report`: reports this Book can have, to offer the person instead; send one as `prompt`, with the same `language`, to build it with no AI.

ReportErrorResponse.description: An error of a report request; with `not_a_report`, `suggestions`; with `empty_book`, `nothing_to_report`, `no_net_result` and `mixed_group`, `problem`: what is involved, and whether the person may organize the Book’s groups.

prompt.description: The report the person asked for, in their own words and language: do not translate it. Include what they said about the period, the view, the chart and a `#hashtag` (only the first is read, as Bkper filters balances by one); leave out the Book’s name or id, which the path gives. Names of the Book’s groups and Accounts written exactly (case and accents aside) are reported as such, several side by side. Uses one Bkper AI decision; a suggestion of `GET /api/v1/books/{bookId}/suggestions`, sent as it is (spacing aside, case kept) with the same `language` (else `Accept-Language`, else English), uses none.
prompt.example: show my expenses by category this year

chart.description: The chart to show, over any the request names: how to show the report, not what it is, so its `text` never names it. `bar`, `line`, `area` or `stacked` by month; `ranked-bar`, `donut` or `pie` of the parts; `compare` (each part against the period compared with); `table` (no chart); `auto` (the report picks). A chart that does not fit the report is not drawn: the report shows the closest chart that fits, else the one it picks, and offers the asked-for chart dimmed with why (`waterfall` never fits). To reopen a report as the person last saw it, send its `text` with its `language` and the chart they chose.

language.description: Language of the report’s texts, as a BCP 47 tag of one of the 133 Bkper languages, such as `pt` or `pt-BR`. Leave it out to write the report in the language of `prompt`, else `Accept-Language`, else English.

format.description: What to return. `html` to show the report to a person: one self-contained, interactive HTML file (`text/html`) that loads nothing and links to the report in the Report app; save it and publish or share it as it is, without asking for `spec` first or re-checking its amounts. `spec` (the default) for JSON, which Report’s own web client renders: the report as a json-render spec with its intent, text, language, query, data time, chart, trace and link.

ReportRequest.description: Exactly one of `prompt` (the person’s request, in any language) or `intent` (from an earlier report, with no AI); a suggestion is sent as `prompt`. Usually `{ "prompt": "…", "format": "html" }`.

prompts.description: All saved prompts in the shelf’s order: a new prompt goes last, and moves change it. The server follows every storage page. Visibility after saves, removals and moves is eventually consistent.

list.description: True for OWNER, EDITOR, POSTER, RECORDER and VIEWER. Unknown or NONE roles are denied.

save.description: True only for OWNER and EDITOR.

remove.description: True only for OWNER and EDITOR; either may remove any prompt on this Book’s shelf.

move.description: True only for OWNER and EDITOR; either may reorder any prompt on this Book’s shelf.

capabilities.description: Freshly authorized capabilities, not a substitute for authorization on the next request. Native saved-query role rules apply; its owner-plan billing restriction is not inherited by app metadata.

id.description: Opaque saved-prompt id returned by this API. Scoped to the Book.

prompt.description: Only the saved request text. To build it against current Book data, send this as `prompt` to the singular POST /api/v1/books/{bookId}/report.

SavedPrompt.description: Book-shared original prompt, not a report snapshot or executable saved query. No HTML, intent, resolved period, amounts, inferred language or separately selected chart is saved.

prompt.description: The original request, in its own words and language. Trimmed at the edges, 1–1000 characters; internal whitespace and case are preserved. No report is computed and no AI is called.

before.description: The id of the saved prompt this one goes just before, or `null` for the end. Take it from the latest list; an id no longer on the shelf answers 409 `shelf_changed`.
